q: What happens to emissions recorded from an e-invoice that was later cancelled?
title: Cancelled e-invoice in carbon records
short: Take them out. A cancelled e-invoice means the sale did not happen on that document, so its quantity is not your activity. If the supplier issued a replacement invoice, count only the replacement. Keep the cancelled file on record, marked as cancelled, so the trail shows why the figure changed.
audience: Accounts teams reconciling carbon records with GST

sections.h: Cancellation and credit notes are different
ul: Cancellation: the supplier can cancel an IRN on the Invoice Registration Portal only within a short window after generating it. The whole invoice falls away. Check the current window in the e-invoice FAQs on the GST e-invoice portal.
Once that window closes the IRN stays live. Corrections then go through a credit note against the original invoice, which may reduce quantity, value or both.
A credit note for returned goods reduces your activity; one for a price discount does not.

sections.h: How to correct your carbon record
ol: Find every line calculated from the cancelled invoice.
Reverse those lines in the same period as the original, since the purchase never happened.
Add the replacement invoice, if any, as a new record with its own number and date.
Write a short note: cancelled IRN, date of cancellation, replacement invoice number.
Do not delete the cancelled file. A verifier will want to see that it was removed on purpose.

p: A reissued invoice usually carries a new document number and often the same goods. Duplicate checks that compare files will treat it as a different document, because it is one. Match replacements by supplier GSTIN, date, goods and quantity, and confirm with the supplier which invoice number stands.

sections.h: If the period is already reported
p: If the cancelled invoice sat in a year you have already published, correct it in the next report and say so. Under the GHG Protocol, an error that changes the base year or a reported total materially is a reason to recalculate; a small one can be fixed going forward with a note.

example.title: Worked example: LPG invoice cancelled and reissued
lines: Cancelled invoice: 20 cylinders x 19 kg = 380 kg LPG; 380 x 2.98 = 1,132.4 kg CO2
Replacement invoice: 18 cylinders x 19 kg = 342 kg; 342 x 2.98 = 1,019.2 kg CO2
Counting both: 1,132.4 + 1,019.2 = 2,151.6 kg, overstated by 1,132.4 kg
example.note: LPG factor is the IPCC 2006 default of 2.98 kg CO2 per kg used by Senseible.

senseible: Senseible gives each file its own SHA-256 fingerprint, so the cancelled invoice and its replacement stay as two separate records, each with its source document. The fingerprint catches identical files; match a reissued invoice with a new number using the checks above.
